description: Repeats 8 Choice questions on one ambiguous post across seven conditions; 99.2% agreement at a 0.60 threshold, flips on 2 of 8 questions
Repeats 14 Noul questions 15 times each on one insurance claim; standard deviation 0.0102, one borderline answer ranging 0.43 to 0.53 across a 0.5 threshold

TypeSafe's own list of nine failure modes: literal reading, counting, numeric and date comparison, indirection, distracting state, adversarial content, contradictory criteria, non-guaranteed invariants, generation. Qualitative, with one numeric example (a Noul and its negation summing to 1.19)
TypeSafe's four-workflow comparison of Jev against frontier models, 61.7% to 76.0% agreement; the reference label is the average of two frontier models, which several independent write-ups criticise

Audits Jev's stated confidence against human-annotated ground truth (civil_comments) rather than another model's opinion: at ~75% stated confidence, only 10% of comments were actually flagged by humans; a 2-parameter recalibration removes 96% of the error
data_and_n: 8,000 judgments (400 comments x 4 questions x wording variants), civil_comments dataset
key_numbers: hard-sample ECE 0.157->0.023 after recalibration; natural-sample ECE 0.209->0.007; AUC ~0.90-0.92 (unchanged by recalibration); wording ECE spans 0.21-0.52
notes: Notes AUC is high (ranking is good) even though calibration is bad, i.e. "calibrated" is technically true by rank correlation (0.96) but misleading for thresholding; ships a companion fix-it tool (jevcal).

description: Calibration-first evaluation of Jev across five RAG mid-pipeline decisions: confidence ranks well (AURC) but is poorly calibrated on retrieval-stopping (ECE 0.33, Brier skill -0.45) yet well-calibrated on chunk-boundary (ECE 0.087, Brier skill +0.21) with the identical backend and harness
data_and_n: HotpotQA n=700 test/300 val; chunk-boundary 119 candidate boundaries + 2 real documents; context-selection n=192 (HotpotQA)/n=300 (SciFact); answer-abstain n=30
key_numbers: Sufficiency: AURC 0.4470, ECE 0.3322, Brier skill -0.4486; chunk-boundary: ECE 0.087, Brier skill +0.21; gated retrieval reduces rounds 38.5% at statistically-tied accuracy
notes: Central finding is that Jev's calibration quality is decision-specific, not one global property; documents statistical testing (McNemar, paired bootstrap) and negative/refused results (e.g. a discarded invalid-ground-truth test) rather than hiding them.

description: Calibration by question type on 8,801 labeled sentiment examples: Noul stated 79.0% vs 72.3% actual, Choice 91.4% vs 76.1%; the 50 to 95% confidence band was only 50 to 57% correct

Calibration study on 8,801 labeled sentiment examples: Jev's raw Noul/Choice probabilities are overconfident (ECE 0.117 for Noul-as-P(positive), worse for Choice), isotonic regression cuts ECE to 0.008, and calibrated Jev beats Llama 3.1-8B at separating right from wrong answers
data_and_n: 8,801 unique labeled sentiment examples (5,280 calibration / 3,521 test)
key_numbers: Raw ECE 0.117 -> Platt 0.052 -> isotonic 0.008; Choice mean confidence 91.4% vs accuracy 76.1% (overconfident); AUROC Jev 0.83 vs Llama 3.1-8B 0.72
notes: Rigorous cross-validated methodology with a held-out test split and a calibration-set-size sweep (20 to 5,280 examples); finds question wording/option order matters little once calibrated.

description: Pulls together the phishing study (62.6% as one question, 95.0% decomposed into five) and the 900-ticket OOD calibration test (ECE 0.107, 4.4x the noise floor); recommends per-question calibration and a none option
Frozen Jev predictions scored for discrimination, calibration and high-recall screening workload on SYNERGY systematic-review data
data_and_n: SYNERGY V1, 10 reviews, 17,191 review-record pairs, 392 eventual inclusions
key_numbers: 17,191 pairs; 392 inclusions; 5,000 bootstrap replicates; 10 reviews
notes: Frozen-prediction release only, no rerun of original inference; labels are final-inclusion not title/abstract adjudication; small review count (10) limits generalization.

description: Independent measurement of Jev as one of three judgment layers, testing whether the self-reported confidence fields track correctness

Browser-automation tool using Jev to pick page elements, with several small measured benchmarks: 41/41 scored element-selection decisions correct across 8 sites (all 30 at p>=0.9 correct), 44/44 in a build-time spike, and loop-mode confidence that does NOT separate correct from wrong decisions (both land p=0.39-0.99)
data_and_n: 30 hand-labelled cases (41 scored) across 8 sites; 44-decision build spike; 3-seed 60s game pilot; n=1 per driving-benchmark task
key_numbers: 41/41 scored correct, 30/30 at p>=0.9; loop-mode: correct decisions p 0.41-0.99, wrong decisions p 0.39-0.47 (no separation); game pilot mean score 3.0 (Jev) vs 0.67 (random); cost ~$0.00004-0.00015/decision
notes: Author repeatedly flags small n, self-graded ground truth, single annotator/easy intents as 'direction, not proof'; explicitly retracts an earlier n=1-per-server speed comparison as unreliable.

description: Ran jev-latest through Mauboussin's 50-question human calibration quiz: 90.0% accuracy at 91.4% mean stated confidence (calibration gap +1.4pts), placing Jev in the top 1.1% of 948 human takers on accuracy and top 7.5% on calibration; 34/34 correct when Jev claimed >=95% confidence
data_and_n: 50 True/False questions (Mauboussin's public calibration quiz), n=948 human comparison baseline
key_numbers: 45/50 correct (90.0%); mean confidence 91.4%, calibration gap +1.4pts, Brier 0.0903, ECE 10.4%; human baseline 60.0% accuracy/+10.0pt overconfidence gap; 34/34 correct at >=95% stated confidence
notes: n=50 items, single run; all 5 errors were classic geographic/statistical illusions also known to trip up humans; results are submitted to and displayed on the quiz's own public leaderboard page.

description: Comparing hand-authored mock probabilities to 28 real Jev calls found the model's real confidence distribution is extreme (mass at 0.0/1.0) and prefers a clean fallback option over picking among wrong choices
data_and_n: 65-item comparison table; 28 real API requests, 29,674 input tokens
key_numbers: $0.00125 total cost for 28 requests; hand-guessed probabilities were high in 18/27 mismatches vs low in 9; confidence frequently exactly 1.0
notes: Author's own framing: this teaches "how to use the programming model," not "whether Jev judges accurately" -- that requires the reader's own data; results tied to jev-1.13.0 and may not hold for other versions.

description: Calibration audit: Jev's chosen-option probabilities are calibrated on CLINC150 (ECE 0.0204) but overconfident on Banking77 (ECE 0.0936), with zero type errors across 8,576 responses
data_and_n: Banking77 + CLINC150(plus), 8,576 responses total
key_numbers: CLINC150 ECE 0.0204 (calibrated); Banking77 ECE 0.0936 (overconfident); 0 type errors
notes: Strong methodological rigor: hash-frozen protocol before any query, independent blind rescorer matched every field; explicitly scopes conclusions to only the artifacts and criteria examined.

description: Jev assigns 82.9% mean probability to its chosen option on a fair 6-sided die (true rate 16.7%) while accuracy stays near chance (19.0%), showing reported probabilities do not reflect known uncertainty
data_and_n: 400-trial die sweep (Choice), smaller coin/Noul/forecast sets (exact n unstated per cell)
model_version: unstated version, via Vercel AI Gateway
key_numbers: Fair die (Choice): expected 16.7%, mean reported 82.9%, accuracy 19.0%; forecast doc stated 45% -> reported 6.6%; stated 55% -> reported 95.9%
notes: Explicitly caveats results are specific to these prompts/conditions and do not establish Jev probabilities are generally unusable.

description: Calibration arena posing questions with analytically known ground-truth probabilities; live Jev scores Brier 0.0059 and ECE 0.0620 on 145 binary events, with a confidence-gated risk-coverage table
data_and_n: 200 trials (145 binary noul events) live run, seed 7
key_numbers: Brier 0.0059, log loss 0.5393, ECE 0.0620 (binary); multiclass Brier 0.1915, ECE 0.109/0.084; d>=0.25 covers 76.6% at 100% accuracy
notes: Live run is stochastic - re-running moves numbers slightly; a live smoke test found Jev assigning 0.89 to a face of a fair die.

description: A sealed-bid auction simulator finds live TypeSafe Jev under-confident on value-threshold probes (ECE 0.1321, Brier 0.1391 vs a perfectly-calibrated oracle's 0.0132/0.0559), causing it to overbid and lose money in second-price auctions
data_and_n: 20 live rounds (13-question fan-out each, 220 probes); 200 offline oracle rounds for comparison
key_numbers: live ECE 0.1321, Brier 0.1391, MAE $43.89; offline oracle ECE 0.0132, Brier 0.0559; live second-price profit -163.4 vs benchmark -7.4 (regret 156.0)
notes: Author notes Jev's coarse choice-band estimate (MAE $26.86) was actually closer than its finer threshold-CDF estimate -- a concrete, stated finding.

description: Applies conformal prediction and prediction-powered inference to Jev's intent-routing confidence on CLINC150; finds the achievable risk bound floors at 1.95% because Jev returns exactly 1.0 confidence on 56.4% of answers (9 of which are wrong)
data_and_n: CLINC150, 2,412 journalled decisions ($0.23 total), 460 calibration/400 held-out
key_numbers: At 5% risk target: 84.75% auto-routed at 2.65% error; alpha=1% infeasible because 56.4% of answers are exactly p=1.0 (9 wrong); PPI++ narrows CI 62% with 40 labels vs 254 labels-only
notes: Extremely rigorous: 43 statistical tests, content-addressed request journal, explicit finding that a 150-way conformal prediction set is useless (averages 148.5/150 labels); documents a deployment case where the certificate catastrophically breaks under distribution shift (loss/query = 1.0000).

description: Research code for 'Calibrated Decisions at Scale': converts police crash narratives to coded variables with pinned jev-1.13.0, audits ECE, Murphy decomposition and calibration slope against coded fields and a human gold set, with a frontier-model baseline
data_and_n: Texas crash narratives; 400-item human gold set
notes: Paper artifact; headline numbers in the paper

description: Jev scored on 5,000 real CDC heart-risk survey respondents vs logistic regression, a chat LLM, and base rate; Jev's AUC trails a chat LLM (0.7725 vs 0.7935) and its stated probabilities are badly miscalibrated (Brier skill -1.315)
data_and_n: CDC BRFSS 2015, 5,000 respondents (253,680 complete-case cohort)
key_numbers: Jev 72.2% acc, AUC 0.7725 vs chat LLM 61.2%/0.7935 vs logistic regression 79.1%/0.8417; Jev Brier skill vs base rate -1.315; cost $0.24 vs $0.68 (LLM)
notes: Explicitly walks back two of its own earlier mistaken conclusions ("Jev beat the LLM," "tied on skill") after a bootstrap rigour review; flags complete-case deletion and label-definition looseness ("heart risk" is really "ever told").

description: Calibration/accuracy benchmark of Jev on 12 public classification tasks (500 ex each); reliability tables show over/under-confidence varies sharply by task (e.g. banking77 0.9-1.0 band: stated 0.98, actual 0.90)
data_and_n: public datasets (Banking77, CLINC150, MASSIVE, LEDGAR, AG News, SMS Spam, QQP, BoolQ, TweetEval, Yelp, CardiffNLP), 500 ex/task, 300/experiment
key_numbers: gate error rate 0.2%-18.4% vs 1.4%-29.6% ungated; OOS median top-prob 0.54 vs 1.00 in-scope, AUROC 0.91; order-shuffle flips 8.7% of answers overall, <2% among p>=0.9
notes: One run, 500 ex/task; label noise in public datasets could depress accuracy/calibration; datasets may be in training data (contamination risk noted).

description: Independent AUROC study of Jev vs DeepSeek Flash and static rules for dependency-update auto-merge decisions; Jev leads in-distribution (AUROC 0.851 vs 0.602/0.585) but its calibrated threshold fails to transfer out-of-distribution (50% precision, 15 unsafe merges on 185 OOD cases)
data_and_n: 1,102 in-distribution cases (BUMP dataset); 185 independent OOD cases (103 repos)
key_numbers: in-dist AUROC 0.851 vs 0.602 (rules)/0.585 (DeepSeek); OOD AUROC 0.605 (95% CI 0.525-0.685); OOD frozen threshold 50.0% precision, 15 unsafe merges of 30 auto-merges
notes: OOD ecosystem-dependent (JS AUROC 0.673 vs non-JS 0.379); OOD outcome-labeling differs from in-distribution (revert-based vs build-failure-based); explicit "does not establish general superiority/inferiority."

description: Tested jev-1.13.0 on 68 probability problems (coins, dice, cards); Noul gives the closest probability estimate (MAE 5.56pp) vs outcome-Choice (MAE 21.14pp); numerical-answer Choice got 60/60 correct when the answer was an offered option
data_and_n: 68 authored scenarios (60 binary + 8 full-distribution), synthetic
key_numbers: Noul MAE 5.56pp vs outcome-Choice 21.14pp; numerical Choice 60/60; Noul+complement summed to 100% off by 7.55pp avg/25pp worst; option-order shift 3.37pp avg
date: 2026-09 (frozen before run; scored 2026-09-22 per docs check)
notes: Small authored suite, single annotator/model version, prompts may interact with textbook-pattern memorization; explicitly not a calibration study across real-world data.

description: Root-causes a known Jev miscalibration (fair-die "choice" collapses to ~77% confidence on one face) and shows it is specific to the Choice primitive: independent Noul questions recover near-true 1/6 probabilities for every face, with severity of Choice's bias scaling with option count
data_and_n: synthetic dice scenarios, n=50 trials per condition, ~10 conditions
key_numbers: choice mean P(face1)=0.769 (true 0.167); noul mean P per face 0.157-0.177 (true 0.167); choice on impossible 7th face 0.038 (ranked above 2 real faces); binary (2-way) choice bias 0.078-0.156 (milder)
notes: Single synthetic scenario family (dice), n=50/condition; author explicitly scopes claim to "evidence about this setting, not a universal claim."

description: 40 hand-labeled tickets, routing, urgency and anger, against Haiku, Fable, Astra and Gemini Flash: routing 97.5%, 8/40 urgency errors; Choice confidence is bimodal while Score confidence clusters mid-range, which makes one threshold unreliable

Coding-agent skill pack measuring Jev's own calibration on 4,995 real decisions (Noul ECE 0.169, Choice ECE 0.226, worse), plus batching cost economics vs Claude (145x/363x cheaper for 256 batched judgments)
data_and_n: 4,995 real Noul decisions; 500 labeled Choice decisions; 102 ranking cases
key_numbers: Noul ECE 0.169; Choice ECE 0.226; 256 judgments cost $0.00049 vs Claude Opus 5 $0.177 (363x); recall@10 0.69-0.83
notes: States TypeSafe has published no calibration curve of its own; raised its own shipped escalate threshold from 0.7 to 0.9 after measuring Choice's miscalibration in the middle of the range.

description: Claude Code hook that judges whether code needs a model at all; separately benchmarks 16 models (incl. Jev) for calibrated binary judgment on 150 passages: Jev is fastest (455ms) and the best-calibrated of the sub-second models, but flags uncertainty 5x more than Haiku
data_and_n: 150 identical passages x16 models (2,400 calls); business-category 149 rows; commit-type 100 rows
key_numbers: Jev 66.0% acc, ECE 0.121, p50 455ms, unsure 34.7%, vs Haiku 66.0% acc, ECE 0.122, 631ms, unsure 2.7%
notes: Also independently checks and finds TypeSafe's own "40-1000x cheaper" claim does not hold at its floor (23.8x cheaper than the cheapest Claude, not 40x).

description: 544 legal documents, 109 labelled yes/no judgments: Brier 0.030; all 96 answers outside the 0.2 to 0.8 band were correct

Byte-identical-prompt bake-off of Laya vs Jev on email-intent classification: both hit 98% on a 100-email holdout, but fine-tuned Laya collapses to 1.00 confidence on its errors while Jev's errors sit at lower confidence, enabling a confidence-based escalation cascade
data_and_n: supplied dataset 2,000 rows (1,210 unique); hand-written holdout n=100
key_numbers: holdout accuracy 98% both models; ECE Jev 0.024 vs fine-tuned Laya 0.021 but Laya wrong-answer confidence is 1.00 on 98/100 rows vs Jev 0.61-0.79; McNemar Jev vs Laya zero-shot p=0.039
notes: n=100 single run/seed (95% CI roughly 93-99.5%); supplied 2,000-row dataset is template-generated with train/test leakage risk if using naive split; only the hand-written holdout is a fair comparison.

description: Measures Jev's behavior when ranking/reranking beyond its per-call limits: probabilities violate IIA (log-odds shift +0.31 to +0.50 with unrelated candidates), 95.8% of a 200-candidate field returns quantized 0.00, and identical repeated calls change 7.3% of a top-10 ranking
data_and_n: BEIR SciFact, 300 test queries, BM25 top-200, chunks of 50
key_numbers: flat nDCG@10 0.7619 vs BM25 0.6617; naive merge nDCG 0.6789 (loses 83% of the gain); anchored 0.7606 at 23% fewer calls; repeat-run top-10 overlap 0.927; shuffled-partition top-10 overlap 0.407
author_type: independent dev (credits systemone/123Satyajeet123 research project for underlying facts)
notes: Single dataset (BEIR SciFact); some strategy-query pairs failed (14/4,144) and are reported, not filtered; predictions were frozen before the run and two of six were refuted.

description: Black-box study of Jev plus controlled replays of the same ~8,300-request suites against open models Laya and SemIf (Qwen3.5-4B)
data_and_n: jev-results: 5 runs, 7,280 total requests; matched replays on Laya and SemIf (7,280 requests each)
key_numbers: accuracy: architecture core 98.86%/86.07%/100%; calibration probability-calibration suite 80.63%/59.41%/74.13% (Jev/Laya/SemIf); binary-prob MAE 0.0793 (Jev) vs 0.2892/0.2526; Jev server time flat 99-167ms across 1-128 questions vs Laya's ~120x growth
notes: Latency measured locally for Laya/SemIf and remotely for Jev, so absolute latency is descriptive, not hardware-normalized; Laya numbers reflect a single specialist checkpoint and SemIf a single model/prompt/runtime.

description: Audio-native 'System One' reproduction (Prosodia) reports that real Jev violates independence of irrelevant alternatives - adding an unrelated option shifts log-odds between two untouched options by ~-0.28 across ten randomized blocks
data_and_n: ten randomized blocks (IIA probe); MELD-based audio benchmark for the reproduced model itself
model_version: real Jev (unspecified version) for the IIA finding; own model for the rest
key_numbers: Jev IIA violation ~ -0.28 log-odds shift, all 10 blocks decreasing
notes: Repo is mainly a model reproduction, not a Jev benchmark; only the IIA section is a direct measurement of real Jev's behavior.

description: TLA+-verified pharmacy-decision consensus kernel wrapping Jev; found Jev is non-deterministic (identical requests returned 0.03-0.04 across 5 calls) and measured distinct noise floors for identity/reorder/paraphrase, with 0 wrong verdicts across 1,080 golden simulated rounds under seeded chaos
data_and_n: 1,490 hash-verified live Jev calls; 1,680 simulated pharmacy decision rounds (14 scenarios x seeds x 3 chaos levels)
key_numbers: noise floors: identity 0.042, reorder 0.059, paraphrase 0.073; calibration on 240 items: acc 0.979, Brier 0.0187, ECE 0.075; 0 wrong verdicts in 1,080 golden rounds (95% CI upper bound 0.28%)
notes: Very rigorous engineering (TLA+ model-checked consensus protocol) but pharmacy scenarios are synthetic/unambiguous by construction, not real clinical data.

description: Compares Jev, GPT-5.6 Luna/Terra and Claude Sonnet 4.6 as agent-eval judges on accuracy, repeat-score variance, cost and latency
data_and_n: 5 frozen weather-agent runs, 100 repetitions each = 500 decisions per judge, 1 human reviewer
key_numbers: Jev 100.0% accuracy vs GPT-5.6 Terra 99.8%, Luna 96.4%, Sonnet 4.6 80.0%; Jev variance 0.0000149 (433x/913x/92x lower than Luna/Terra/Sonnet); Jev /bin/bash.00035/call, 0.44s latency
notes: Small corpus (5 runs, 1 human reviewer); authors state result is not a general judge-accuracy ranking.

description: 500/500 agreement with a human oracle across repeated runs; per-case variance 92x to 913x lower than GPT-5.6 and Claude Sonnet comparators
Adversarial browser-exploration tool found narrow oracle questions score far better than broad ones (0.99 vs 0.30) and the same page state can score 0.72-0.87 across repeat calls
data_and_n: Demo app with planted bugs; specific findings from live calibration runs (exact n unstated)
key_numbers: Untranslated-key example scored 0.30 (broad question) vs 0.99 (narrow question); repeat-call score range 0.72-0.87 on identical state
notes: Documents two concrete false-positive causes traced to missing context (browser validation tooltip, SQLi payload echoed back) rather than model error; states judgments are text-only, so visual/layout bugs are a blind spot.

description: Jev vs Cohere Rerank 3.5 as a RAG reranker on 1,044 Turkish XQuAD questions; both recover the identical number of gold passages into top-5, with Jev 60.6% cheaper, but a candidate-order permutation audit shows real sensitivity (mean Spearman 0.262)
data_and_n: XQuAD-TR, n=1,044 questions, 240-passage corpus
key_numbers: Recall@5 99.425% (Jev = Cohere); nDCG 98.097 (Jev) vs 98.626 (Cohere); cost -60.6%; order-audit mean Spearman rho 0.262, mean top-5 Jaccard 0.288
notes: Using Jev as the sole first-stage retriever was explicitly "rejected" (far worse than BM25); candidate-order sensitivity is flagged as a real limitation, not fixed by default.

description: 282-trial harness testing Jev's documented claims via OpenRouter: batching independence confirmed to the digit, repeat stability (sd<=0.0075), but option-order reshuffling shifted a winning probability 0.62->0.48 and uncovered inputs answered wrong at >0.93 confidence
data_and_n: 282 trials (one full committed run); calibration subset n=20
key_numbers: 282/282 structural invariants clean; latency flat 403-431ms for 1-30 questions; option reorder moved winning probability 0.62->0.48; 2/3 out-of-taxonomy inputs wrong at confidence>=0.93; Chinese-question agreement 0.79 vs 0.92 (English)
notes: Every finding reproducible offline from a committed raw-response log; distinguishes "hypothesis" (author-guessed) from "documented fact" (must reproduce) expectations in its own framework.

description: Jev-powered pairwise "fuzzy sort" library; a live 100-ticket benchmark got 92.85-98.38% pairwise-ordering agreement with a stated priority policy, and found non-transitive judgments
data_and_n: 100 synthetic support tickets, live benchmark; small live/mocked tests otherwise
key_numbers: default batches 16.60s/92.85% agreement; batch-16 concurrency-4 12.83s/98.38% agreement; top-10 always correct, full order never exact
notes: Single runs on a controlled synthetic fixture, explicitly "not performance or accuracy guarantees"; notes AI judgments can be non-transitive (cyclic).

description: Jev vs GPT-4.1 as synthetic survey respondents on Twin-2K-500; asked as Noul, Jev beats GPT-4.1 probabilities on all 6 measures at 1/34 the cost, but as Choice it loses the headline distribution-gap metric
data_and_n: Twin-2K-500, 300 respondents x 108 questions = 24,596 cells per arm
key_numbers: Noul: dist. gap 0.1530 vs GPT-4.1 0.1789, ECE 0.1472 vs 0.2393, cost $4.02 vs ~$136; Choice: dist. gap 0.1985 (worse than GPT-4.1)
notes: Author flags the Noul arm was built after seeing the Choice result (post-hoc), and that a stricter pre-specified per-column test favors GPT-4.1 (p=0.9995); calibration misses its own 0.05 bar for every arm.

description: Context-compaction plugin found noul-style judgments unreliable on subjective questions (0.996 on hard facts vs 0.003-0.28 on judgment calls) and that a statement and its negation both scored ~0.95 with noul, fixed by switching to explicit-criteria choice questions
data_and_n: unstated for noul/choice test; 40 tickets for the Jev-vs-Laya comparison
model_version: Laya (local) primarily; hosted Jev cited for comparison
key_numbers: noul reliability 0.996 (fact) vs 0.003-0.28 (judgment); negation pair both scored ~0.95 with noul, 0.75-0.99 with choice; hosted Jev 78% vs Laya 57% on 40 ambiguous tickets
notes: Most measurements are against local Laya, not hosted Jev; the Jev-vs-Laya comparison is explicitly flagged as a small, directional sample.

description: Runtime rule-enforcement layer for a coding agent that uses Jev for narrow judgments; measured findings include calibrated-but-slightly-underconfident probabilities, flat latency across question count, and strong anchoring on field order
data_and_n: 70 labelled items, 108 cross-kind pairs, 49 benchmark sessions; scripted benchmark 79 sessions/261 decisions; replay of 21 real sessions/9,090 tool calls
key_numbers: Calibration: p 0.9-1.0 -> 98% true, p 0-0.1 -> 7% true; latency flat at 1/4/8 Qs (274/273/276ms); go-ahead detection 71%->93% after question redesign; benchmark recall 71.4%->98.5% across versions
notes: Explicitly documents a finding that reversed an earlier conclusion (question-format helps some judgments, hurts others); cost negligible (~$0.00004/session, ~1.7 calls).

description: Judge-repeatability study scoring 12 frozen agent-run cases 100x each; Jev repeats its verdicts fully while 3 LLM judges (deepseek/gemini/gpt) show real run-to-run variance, none beating a majority-class baseline on binary evals, even with sampling off
data_and_n: 12 frozen cases x 3 evals x 4 judges x 100 repetitions (14,400 decisions); matched (sampling-off) and frontier (claude-opus-5/gpt-5.6-sol) arms
key_numbers: cost/1,000 traces $0.49 (Jev) vs $6.56-$259.70 (LLM judges, list price); Jev fully repeats itself; gpt-5.6-luna still disagrees with itself at temperature 0
notes: Labels are one person's single reading of 12 cases; 11/12 cases positive on both binary evals, so majority-class baseline scores 91.7% itself.

description: Jev and Laya (zero-shot) vs classic trained ML on three Kaggle datasets; Jev is competitive on AG News/tweets but far behind trained models on Titanic, and is measurably non-deterministic (probability shifts up to 0.13 on repeat queries)
data_and_n: AG News 120k train/7.6k test; Disaster Tweets 7,613 (80/20); Titanic 891 (80/20)
key_numbers: AG News: Jev 88.1% vs Laya 92.8% vs LogReg 92.6%; Tweets: Jev 81.6% vs LogReg 79.9%; Titanic: LogReg 84.4% vs Jev 71.5% vs Laya 61.5%; repeat-query prob changed in 46% of tweets (max d0.12), 80% of Titanic rows (max d0.13)
notes: Written in Portuguese; calibration is poor outside AG News (Jev ECE 0.074 there); prompt wording tuned outside the test set on a 500-row dev split.

description: DuckDB extension gating semantic SQL functions on Jev's calibration; a 6-condition calibration/invariant gate (Brier, ECE, negation symmetry, rubric ordinality) on 360 fresh live requests, 5 of 6 passing
data_and_n: 360 rows, 350 fresh requests (~999 tokens/row) on a 20-Newsgroups-derived corpus
key_numbers: bool ECE 0.0454 (gate <=0.10, pass); choice accuracy 0.8754; score on-topic/off-topic inversion 0.0370; model systematically underconfident (+0.042 mean signed gap)
notes: Explicitly separates negation-specific effects from general wording sensitivity via a paraphrase control (finds negation result "not about negation"); flags that within-topic ordinal ranking is untested.

description: Measures whether ORDER BY over a Jev probability gives a defensible sort: passes all 6 pre-registered gates on 360 labeled rows (inversion 0.036) but fails 4 of 6 on a harder Amazon-ESCI product-ranking probe (inversion 0.255), and batching 40 rows/request breaks the gate that passes
data_and_n: 360 human-labeled rows; Amazon ESCI 306 pairs / 30 hard queries
key_numbers: Main: bool ECE 0.045, inversion 0.036; ESCI hard probe: bool ECE 0.242, inversion 0.255; 53/360 rows tie at probability 0.99
notes: Explicitly built because three DuckDB/Postgres Jev ORDER BY integrations ship no such measurement; batching materially changes whether the ranking gate passes.

description: Fuzzer that renames/reorders question IDs, Choice options and JSON keys and checks whether Jev's decision changes; measured run found six confirmed robustness violations out of 100 mutations across 10 states
data_and_n: 10 states, 100 mutations
key_numbers: Live results: 10 states, 100 mutations, 6 confirmed violations (e.g. reversing JSON key order flips a relevance judgment)
notes: Explicitly states a PASS does not prove the original answer was correct, only that it was stable; suspected failures are rerun to separate genuine instability from single-call flukes.

description: Qwen3 8B vs Jev 1.13.0 vs Laya CoreML on 24 typed decisions (choice/noul/score), each repeated 10x: Jev and Qwen are both 100% label-consistent across repeats, but Jev is far slower (808-848ms vs 6-100ms)
data_and_n: 24 decisions (8 choice, 8 noul, 8 score) x10 repeats (240 executions per model)
key_numbers: Jev 100% accuracy on the 8-item pilot; 240/240 success, 0 hard-label flips across repeats, mean probability std 0.000525; p50 808-847ms vs Qwen 98-101ms vs Laya 6-8ms

description: Jev vs Claude Haiku on 2,000 phishing emails: single verdict 62.6% vs 81.3% accuracy, but Jev's 5 decomposed signal questions fed into a logistic regression reach 95.0% vs Haiku's 93.2% (not statistically significant)

description: Jev integration notes: 60 multilingual routing phrases show 0 confidently-wrong answers (all misses flagged low-confidence), splitting one decision into 3 questions destroys calibration (0.55/0.42 vs merged 1.00), and Jev drives a QA walk 6.9-13.8x cheaper than a vision model

description: Counterfactual fairness benchmark: swaps 29 demographic attributes (140 levels) one at a time across 10 high-stakes decision scenarios (hiring, lending, bail, clinical triage, etc.) on Jev (11,984 calls) and Claude Opus 5 (2,984 calls), measuring which swaps move the decision beyond the model's own noise

description: Ports LLM prompting techniques (CoT, self-consistency, few-shot, GEPA) to Jev via DSPy and measures effect across LegalBench, BBH, MMLU-Pro and CLERC; most 'reasoning' techniques do nothing since Jev has no scratchpad

notes: Separates 'information-carrying' techniques (which help) from 'reasoning' techniques (which don't, since Jev has no scratchpad); option-order self-consistency within noise.

description: Financial anomaly-detection gate using Jev resists an in-memo prompt-injection bait (99% probability circuit-breaker trip) and beats GLM 5.3 Flash 8-23x on latency/cost at matching verdicts across attack scenarios; 100% deterministic verdicts and token counts over 5 repeats

notes: Explicitly states the benchmark does not prove Jev makes better classification choices than GLM, only that it is faster/cheaper at matching verdicts.

description: Falsification-first study of Jev as a capability router: confidence-gating AUC 0.44 (inverted, falsified) and 13/13 resistance to adversarial near-duplicate candidates

description: Confidence-gated Jev-then-LLM routing measured on 600 MASSIVE utterances: Jev is well-calibrated (ECE 4.5%, AUROC 0.83), but escalation buys no net accuracy since GPT-5.2 is no better on this task, and under prompt injection GPT-5.2 is flipped 100/80 times by one payload vs 26/80 for Jev

description: Jev classifying agent tool-call risk (readonly/destructive/privileged/exfiltration) on 60 hand-labeled cases including adversarially-worded destructive commands: 91.7% accuracy, and every wrong answer carried hedged confidence

notes: No frontier-LLM baseline collected yet (adapters exist but unrun, so latency/cost are not comparative); run-to-run accuracy varied 91.7-93.3% across repeats.

Preregistered adversarial evaluation of jev-1.13.0 (123,805 requests): calibration holds on support routing (ECE 0.075) but collapses on random 3-SAT (P(satisfiable) barely moves despite true rate spanning 0 to 1); batching 60 questions is 20x cheaper/8x faster with identical answers

notes: Plan written from documentation/press before probing revealed API differs from docs in 3 ways; raw logs published separately; explicitly notes some formal tasks are off-distribution for a decision model.

description: Pre-registered study on 486 Wikipedia deletion discussions finds Jev 1.13.0 96.5% accurate/0.230 ECE at baseline, collapses to 26.5% accuracy under a one-line prompt injection, and shows a mirrored-question probability gap

notes: Pre-registered design with placebo band and multiple-comparison correction; author flags own limitations (486 vs planned 500 items, single task/version).

description: JEV vs GPT/Llama/Qwen/xLAM on tool-selection and abstention benchmarks (MetaTool, When2Call, BFCL); JEV leads BFCL relevant-action accuracy (87.50%) and abstains best on MetaTool, but hallucinates a tool call on 76% of When2Call's no-tool cases

notes: Notes state-blind baseline scores 0.38-0.46 vs 0.15 chance, a caution for anyone benchmarking this model; explicit noise-floor correction methodology for ECE at small n.

description: Calibration test of Jev on 3 public benchmarks plus a contamination-free synthetic rule task; synthetic ECE is 4.4x the noise floor and the unknowable-label question is confidently wrong

description: Jev answers all 58,492 public BBQ bias-benchmark questions at 97.28% accuracy (99.96% on ambiguous, 94.60% on informative), with position-reversal changing only 1/484 paired answers

description: Six-track stress test of Jev (~8,400 calls): confirms documented API limits exactly, finds it overconfident at low confidence bands but well-calibrated above 0.9, largely immune to prompt injection, and unable to count/sort/add

notes: Very broad single-run robustness probe; explicitly documents that Jev "can't add, sort dates, or count."

description: 1,000-decision benchmark across 25 reasoning families; Jev scores 97-100% on static/relational logic tasks but only 13.2% on sequential state-mutation tasks and 33.3% on exact truth-counting, while its stated confidence is highly predictive (>=0.95 correct 492/493 times)

description: Twelve field tests plus follow-ups on Jev: 89% accuracy/0.03 ECE on 400 BoolQ items, overconfident 4-way calibration (0.998 stated vs 0.90 actual), counting/date weaknesses, and 27/28 SQL-injection and guardrail detection

key_numbers: 82.3% [79.0,85.2] vs local baseline 27.0%; question-deleted accuracy drops 32.5pp; ECE 0.025; both math sections net-negative (-1.25) on official scoring

description: Two capability-boundary probes on Jev: chess (worse-than-random from a raw FEN board, ~950 Elo once given hand-computed tactical facts) and NPC-addressee detection (F1 0.96 clean text, 0.93 noisy speech-to-text)

key_numbers: Chess: FEN-only 533cp mean loss (worse than random 403cp) vs tactical-facts 90cp; ~950 Elo estimate; addressee F1 0.962/0.944/0.927 clean/stt/misheard
notes: Extremely detailed, self-critical methodology; explicit about small samples (n=30, n=79) and that addressee ground truth is hand-labeled by the author.

description: Recorded Jev answers matched hand-authored expectations only 6/27 at first; literal-reading and compound-question bugs fixed, reaching 27/28 after 3 iterations

key_numbers: agreement 6/27 to 14/28 to 19/28 to 27/28; batching measured 12.2x cheaper, 10.0x faster; one compound-question fix alone moved 14/28 to 19/28
notes: Explicit literal-reading failure (security-label word "untrusted" triggered a veto on unrelated inputs); Score-vs-Choice confidence semantics bug found and fixed; a live 529-overload retry path documented.

description: Jev's accuracy and calibration in Russian vs English on XNLI (n=600 paired): accuracy 77.3% vs 88.3%, ECE 0.096 vs 0.032; traced to a cross-lingual entailment-recognition failure, not tokenization or length
data_and_n: XNLI n=600 x15 languages (3 studies); MASSIVE n=600; Belebele n=900; SIB-200 n=204/lang
key_numbers: XNLI RU-EN paired Δacc -11.0pp [-14.2,-7.8]; ΔECE +0.063; all 14/14 non-English languages worse on XNLI; MASSIVE/Belebele/SIB-200 show no cross-lingual loss
notes: Pre-registered across three studies with paired bootstrap CIs; single model version (jev-1.13.0), option keys kept English as a deliberate control.

description: 480 authored Persian (Farsi + Finglish) questions across 10 linguistic/pragmatic categories run against Jev 1.13.0: 99.6% Choice accuracy, 99.4% Noul, 95.0% Score, with perfect repeatability and English-vs-Persian parity
data_and_n: 480 questions (624 total evaluations incl. diagnostics), 80 authored scenarios
key_numbers: Choice 239/240 (99.6%, Brier 0.0112); Noul 159/160 (99.4%); Score 76/80 (95.0%, MAE 0.0709 levels); 0 decision changes across 48 three-observation repeat groups
notes: Includes explicit cost comparison to 4 other models by token-matched estimate (Jev 1.0x, Claude Haiku 4.5 56.6x, GPT 12.6x); author-written gold answers, not independently reviewed.

description: 100-question-per-cell sample check of Jev in Korean vs English and vs GPT-5.6 Luna across 4 public exams; Korean reading comprehension shows no meaningful cost, but Jev trails Luna by 8pp on the Korean medical exam

key_numbers: Belebele: Jev 96/100 KO vs 97/100 EN; KorMedMCQA: Jev 80/100 vs Luna 88/100 (+8pp, 95% CI [2,15]); order-sensitivity flip rate 13% KO / 14% EN; latency 221ms vs Luna 1085ms
notes: Explicitly labeled a 'sample check,' not a benchmark, with ±8pp uncertainty per 100-item cell; notes ~2% answer variance on identical re-run requests limiting exact reproducibility.

description: Spanish-language audit: swapping only the input text from English to Spanish costs Jev 3.0-6.4pp accuracy and roughly doubles calibration error on the hardest two of four datasets; writing instructions in Spanish does not help
data_and_n: XNLI 1000, PAWS-X 1000, MASSIVE 600, Belebele 600 (n=3,200 paired items)
key_numbers: XNLI acc EN 0.850 -> ES 0.786 (-6.4pp, CI[-8.6,-4.3]); XNLI ECE 0.057->0.101; Spanish costs 17-38% more input tokens; stability check accuracy jitter 0.000-0.005 vs deltas of 0.030-0.064
notes: Explicit single-wording-per-cell caveat: the null result for Spanish instructions is about these two wordings, not proof instructions are interchangeable in general; compares directly against a prior Russian-language audit.

description: Typed client + benchmark harness for Jev; the shipped example run against 15 real-project fixtures gets 81.7% overall accuracy but shows one question ('needs_human', an indirect compound judgment) scoring 46.7% - worse than a coin flip - which the harness itself flags

key_numbers: overall accuracy 81.7% (49/60); needs_human 46.7% (7/15); at confidence>=0.7 threshold: 60% coverage at 100% accuracy; p50 latency 809ms; TypeSafe's own benchmark cited: Jev 67.8% vs GPT-5.6 Sol 74.1%

description: CLI that grades whether a Jev question's answers are usable against labels; on its bundled example, vague criteria scored 0.69-0.89 accuracy and rewritten criteria reached 0.92-1.00 with holdout AUC up to 1.00

description: Runtime-assurance library for Jev decision workflows: derives Jev's confidence-margin formula from live traces, measures batched-vs-separate-request distribution shift, and finds paired requests are 34.7% cheaper and 49.4% faster than separate calls
data_and_n: 1,490 hash-verified live API calls (measurement examples); production trace examples (351 decisions cited for the console demo)
key_numbers: batched-question JS divergence 0.0058 vs 0.0035 (near-identical to same request); paired requests 34.7% cheaper, 49.4% faster; a live schema-repair example: decision test p=0.25 vs probability test p=0.031
notes: Primarily a monitoring/tooling library, but its documented findings (confidence formula, batching independence, cost/speed) are real live-API measurements, not just claims.

description: Evidence-ledger meta-analysis recomputing every published Jev ECE against its sampling noise floor, plus original experiments; finds Jev's probabilities are miscalibrated 2.1-2.5x the noise floor at every difficulty tier and are quantized to 0.01 (can return exact 0 or 1)
data_and_n: 800-item difficulty gradient (Noul questions); cross-domain slices 480 items in 4 domains; negation probe n=80
key_numbers: ECE 2.1-2.5x noise floor across all 4 tiers; exact p=1.0/0.0 possible (Noul never did in 2,580 answers); Platt-slope transfer cuts ECE 74% with ~50 labels; batching cost ~0.33ms/extra question
date: started September 2026, maintained as living ledger
notes: Notably meta in scope (recomputes other repos' published ECE figures against noise floors, e.g. flags a widely-cited n=60 benchmark as unable to measure calibration at all); every claim tracked with source/status in a public ledger.

description: Bilingual capability atlas synthesizing own tests and third-party benchmarks into an axis of "signal-sufficient vs needs-external-knowledge"; own tests include a history-recall miscalibration case (0.90 confidence on a wrong answer after a typo) and measured intent-classification ECE 0.041
data_and_n: Various small own probes (citation-support, sarcasm, history-recall) plus cited external benchmarks (AG News, Banking77, DAIR Emotion)
key_numbers: Own measured ECE 0.041 (Chinese intent classification); history-recall confidence 0.90 on a wrong answer, 1.00 after correcting a typo; cited DAIR Emotion 48% accuracy at 0.819 mean confidence
notes: Explicitly framed as a synthesis/field-guide, not a leaderboard; every claim tagged by evidence tier (own test / third-party / official doc / own judgment); publicly corrected an earlier version after a reader-reported error.
